rule: One claim per substantive statement of fact or behavior in the candidate's CHANGELOG.md [0.25.0] section; restatements share an id; no claim the notes do not make. R2 reads {"claims": ["claim:<id>", ...]} (scripts/verify_release_adjudication.py claim_registry).

source.lineCoordinates: details.*.lines are 1-based line numbers in the rendered notes; line 1 is the section header.

notRegistered: Lines 1-2 (header), 9, 13, 39, 41-43, 54-59, 106, 113, 153, 157, 191-193, 204-206, 259, 279, 302, 315, 324, 345, 366-368, 404-406 are headers, blank lines or framing text that restate a registered claim or make none.

claim:freeze-notes-before-a1.text: The notes were frozen with the candidate on 2026-10-20, before A1 (#1430); a release publishes only after A1 accepts the candidate, and the notes cannot change after the freeze.
claim:freeze-notes-before-a1.plain: The release notes were fixed when the candidate was frozen and cannot change.

claim:freeze-nothing-released.text: At the freeze there was no v0.25.0 tag, NuGet package or GitHub release; the newest NuGet release was 0.24.0.
claim:freeze-nothing-released.plain: Nothing of 0.25 had been published at the freeze.

claim:freeze-no-family-ready.text: At the freeze the scope packet recorded 0 of 6 families ready; a family is ready only when its cases pass on the frozen candidate and the maintainer approves; the per-family results in the notes were measured before the freeze.
claim:freeze-no-family-ready.plain: At the freeze no family was marked ready; readiness is decided after the freeze, by this review.

claim:reproof-required-no-024-reuse.text: Because #1408 ended MILESTONE-FAILED, the candidate must re-pass 0.24's proof, provenance and release checks on its own commit; no 0.24 approval or record is reused.
claim:reproof-required-no-024-reuse.plain: 0.24's failed review means 0.25 had to redo 0.24's checks on its own code.

claim:candidate-refrozen-once.text: The first candidate (2026-10-19) failed the re-proof: its determinism run found no disagreement but one macOS runner hit its 50-minute limit; F2-INTERP-09's counts predated other merges; F4-ITER-04 cannot be measured. The maintainer amended all three (70-minute limit, counts re-registered, F4-ITER-04 not measured) and the candidate was re-frozen on 2026-10-20.
claim:candidate-refrozen-once.plain: The first frozen candidate failed the re-check, three rules were amended, and the candidate was frozen again.

claim:release-gaps-closed.text: #1545, #1546 and #1547 closed on 2026-10-19, before the freeze; acceptance requires them closed. The release gate (#1410) lets a release publish only with an adjudication identity: the accepted commit plus the hash of its record.
claim:release-gaps-closed.plain: The three release-process gaps left by 0.24 were closed before the freeze, and publishing needs the review's identity.

claim:reduced-independence.text: Codex reviewed each change and the maintainer approved and merged it; no reviewer independent of the two took part, so every 0.25 evidence claim is at most bounded.
claim:reduced-independence.plain: Only Codex and the maintainer reviewed 0.25; nothing here is a stronger claim than 'bounded'.

claim:known-open-defects.text: A private base-class member named @default makes a converted out var fail to compile with CS0122 (#1573), a loud failure. Reading a field of a struct array element still needs --permissive-effects.
claim:known-open-defects.plain: Two known converter limitations ship with 0.25, and both fail visibly.

claim:no-new-benchmark-results.text: This release publishes no new benchmark results.

claim:native-local-functions.text: A §F inside a §F or §MT body is a local function, emitted in place as a C# static local function; its name is visible in the whole body and wins over a same-named method in bare calls; it cannot capture (CS8421); its effects are charged to the enclosing callable; other placements and shapes, and value uses in unchecked-effect positions, are rejected with the new Calor0211.
claim:native-local-functions.plain: Calor gains local functions (functions declared inside functions), with a new error Calor0211 for unsupported forms.

claim:local-functions-convert-natively.text: Non-capturing C# local functions declared directly in a method body (without the listed modifiers and parameter kinds) convert to a nested §F; F3-LOCAL-01 to 03 convert natively on all 8 measured surfaces, compile with default options and print the same result; other local functions stay §CSHARP and are reported as local-function, now Partial.
claim:local-functions-convert-natively.plain: The converter turns simple C# local functions into Calor local functions; the rest stay C#.

claim:calor0212-invalid-by-reference-ope.text: Passing something C# cannot pass by reference (literal, computed value, call result, property, indexer element, this, readonly field outside its constructor, in parameter as ref/out) is now Calor0212 instead of a C# compile failure (Calor1002).
claim:calor0212-invalid-by-reference-ope.plain: Bad ref/out/in arguments are now caught by Calor with a clear error.

claim:by-ref-more-operands-compile.text: Array elements and fields through a receiver compile as ref/out/in operands in module functions; §A{out} _ is a discard, rejected with Calor0212 when a variable named _ is in scope.
claim:by-ref-more-operands-compile.plain: More kinds of ref/out arguments now compile.

claim:by-ref-writes-charge-mut.text: Passing an array element, field through a receiver, or dotted path as ref or out charges mut like §ASSIGN; the effect-laundering bug where a §E{alloc} function wrote through ref is fixed and such code now fails with Calor0410.
claim:by-ref-writes-charge-mut.plain: Writes through ref/out now count as mutations for effect checking, closing a loophole.

claim:by-ref-null-checks-end-earlier.text: In functions with two or more by-reference parameters a write to one ends null checks on the others; with one or more, any call, construction, or field/element/property read ends them; code relying on the old behavior reports Calor0272.
claim:by-ref-null-checks-end-earlier.plain: Null checks are invalidated sooner when by-reference parameters may share storage.

claim:convert-keeps-by-ref-identity.text: calor convert passes a struct-array element's field itself for Bump(ref pts[0].X); out var becomes a mutable binding declared before the statement in the listed positions when its type is known and its name is free, starting at default; other forms keep their statement or member as C#.
claim:convert-keeps-by-ref-identity.plain: Converted ref/out code keeps writing to the same storage, and out var is lowered safely or left as C#.

claim:by-ref-shapes-stay-csharp.text: Ref locals and returns, conditional refs, scoped and ref readonly parameters, this ref/this in extension calls, by-reference delegates and lambdas, by-reference constructor and indexer arguments, calls omitting in, and method-generic out T stay C#; flow attributes are copied but not used by null checks; a C# ref argument to an in parameter converts to §A{in}.
claim:by-ref-shapes-stay-csharp.plain: By-reference forms Calor cannot express are kept as C#.

claim:feature-check-by-ref-entries.text: calor feature-check: out-var is Partial; ref-parameter and out-parameter no longer suggest tuples or Result; in-parameter names the call sites that stay C#; ref-expression and multidim-array no longer claim full conversion.
claim:feature-check-by-ref-entries.plain: The feature-check report now describes ref/out support accurately.

claim:by-ref-corpus-effect.text: Over MediatR, Serilog and FluentValidation, 33 more members and types are kept as C# (31 out var that cannot be lowered, 2 method-generic out T); binder-visited expressions drop from 35,177 to 34,371 (2.3%), a count that does not measure native conversion; 10 more of 364 modules reach effect checking.
claim:by-ref-corpus-effect.plain: On three real libraries, 33 more members stay C#, and 10 more of 364 modules get further through the compiler.

claim:by-ref-contract-cases-hold.text: Tests compile every contract case and compare convert/compile/run on the CLI, migrate and MCP paths; all 57 Calor contract cases hold; witness D1-LV-03 was corrected by a contract amendment and now reports Calor0212. Separately, one case stays open: a struct array element's field read still needs --permissive-effects.
claim:by-ref-contract-cases-hold.plain: All 57 ref/out contract cases hold; one conversion limitation stays open.

claim:interp-overload-selection-kept.text: calor convert wraps FormattableString and IFormattable interpolation targets in an explicit cast, so the converted program calls the same overload; before, a FormattableString-only method failed to compile and the CLI kept the class as C#.
claim:interp-overload-selection-kept.plain: Interpolated strings keep calling the same overload after conversion.

claim:interp-handlers-kept-as-csharp.text: Calls whose target is an [InterpolatedStringHandler] type, FormattableString.Invariant($"text") and handler concatenations keep their enclosing statement or member as C# interop on every surface.
claim:interp-handlers-kept-as-csharp.plain: Special interpolated-string targets are kept as C# instead of being miscompiled.

claim:interp-holes-native-subset.text: Holes of the listed forms convert natively; a digit-only hole is written ${INT:1}; other holes keep their C# text as §CS{...} and count as interop.
claim:interp-holes-native-subset.plain: Only simple interpolation holes are converted; others are kept as marked C#.

claim:interp-hole-evaluation-order.text: A hole containing a string literal is no longer hoisted into a temporary ahead of the statement.
claim:interp-hole-evaluation-order.plain: Interpolation holes now run in the original order.

claim:interp-holes-analyzed.text: A C#-form call inside a hole is an ordinary call for effect checking; a pure function containing one now fails with Calor0410 instead of a Calor0419 warning; other hole forms still warn.
claim:interp-holes-analyzed.plain: Effects inside interpolation holes are now checked, which can turn a warning into an error.

claim:interp-hole-diagnostic-location.text: An error inside a hole is reported at the hole's line and column instead of 1:1.
claim:interp-hole-diagnostic-location.plain: Errors in interpolation holes point to the right place.

claim:interp-feature-check-entries.text: string-interpolation is Partial; new entries string-interpolation-to-string (Full), -formattable and -hole (Partial), -handler and -formattable-constant (NotSupported).
claim:interp-feature-check-entries.plain: feature-check lists interpolation support in more detail.

claim:interp-checked-by-differential-tes.text: These are checked by convert, compile and run tests that compare output with the original C# on the CLI and MCP settings, including de-DE and fr-FR.
claim:interp-checked-by-differential-tes.plain: Interpolation conversion is tested by running both programs and comparing output, also in German and French locales.

claim:report-label-fixed.text: calor convert no longer prints '(N via --passthrough fallback)' for default rescues; it prints the preservation paths line shown.
claim:report-label-fixed.plain: The convert report no longer mislabels automatic rescues as passthrough.

claim:report-path-trigger-fields.text: Each recorded loss has path; rescues and passthroughs also have trigger and enabledBy; a per-file conversionPaths object (schema 1) gives outcome, per-path counts, triggers and option state; all fields are additive.
claim:report-path-trigger-fields.plain: Conversion reports say which mechanism kept each member as C# and why.

claim:mcp-module-name-rescue-fixed.text: MCP calor_convert with moduleName or inputPath, and calor_batch with moduleNameOverride, now rescue global-namespace types like other calls.
claim:mcp-module-name-rescue-fixed.plain: A custom module name no longer breaks the MCP rescue.

claim:mcp-roundtrip-honours-passthrough.text: calor_convert in roundtrip mode honours passthroughOnError and returns a lossSummary.
claim:mcp-roundtrip-honours-passthrough.plain: An MCP option that was ignored is now honoured.

claim:batch-abort-json.text: A calor_batch abort with skipOnError false returns JSON with error, preservationPaths and per-file conversionPaths; isError stays true.
claim:batch-abort-json.plain: A batch abort now returns structured JSON.

claim:surface-defaults-unchanged.text: Defaults differ by surface (convert rescues round-trip failures; calor_convert and the library do not and say so; migrate, calor_migrate and calor_batch rescue only unparseable Calor); no default changed in this release.
claim:surface-defaults-unchanged.plain: Each conversion surface's defaults are now documented; none changed.

claim:json-verbose-stdout-single-documen.text: With --format json --verbose, convert, verify and benchmark no longer print progress text to stdout; tests pin the contract for every command with both options.
claim:json-verbose-stdout-single-documen.plain: JSON output stays parseable when --verbose is used.

claim:assess-coverage-by-ref-description.text: calor assess and calor coverage (and MCP analysis tools) no longer describe ref/out/out var as unsupported; construct names and counts and scores are unchanged.
claim:assess-coverage-by-ref-description.plain: Analysis commands describe ref/out support correctly.

claim:expression-bodied-compound-assignm.text: void M() => Log += s; converts to a compound assignment instead of Log = s.
claim:expression-bodied-compound-assignm.plain: A silent operator loss in conversion is fixed.

claim:local-shadows-function-in-calls.text: When the innermost declaration of a call's name is a local or parameter, the binder treats the call as a delegate invocation, as C# does.
claim:local-shadows-function-in-calls.plain: Calls now resolve to a local delegate before a same-named function, matching C#.

claim:double-literals-kept.text: Whole-number double literals stay floating-point in conversion (2.0), including attribute arguments, and default(float)/default(decimal) keep their width (#1528).
claim:double-literals-kept.plain: The converter no longer turns 2.0 into 2, which changed division results.

claim:iterator-accessors-preserved.text: Iterator getters (yield in a property or indexer) are kept whole as §CSHARP with an iterator-accessor loss on convert, migrate, MCP and the library, with or without passthrough, compiling with default options; laziness, finally-on-dispose and exception timing match in 2 of 2 fixtures on 6 surfaces; --no-fallback fails naming the feature; one registered case (F4-ITER-04) is not measured; iterator methods still convert to §YIELD.
claim:iterator-accessors-preserved.plain: C# iterator properties are kept as C# instead of producing illegal Calor; one test case could not be measured.

claim:partial-properties-preserved.text: Every C# 13 partial property or indexer declaration is kept as §CSHARP with a partial-property loss (iterator-accessor when a same-file part yields).
claim:partial-properties-preserved.plain: Partial properties are kept as C# instead of breaking the build.

claim:named-refinement-arithmetic.text: Operators see a named refinement type (§RTYPE) as its base type; results have the base type except inc/dec of a variable; writes back into refined targets are still checked; binding a plain base value to a refined §B is still rejected (#1515).
claim:named-refinement-arithmetic.plain: Arithmetic on named refinement types now type-checks.

claim:decimal-arithmetic-type.text: decimal + decimal is typed decimal; assigning it to i32 is Calor0202; nested decimal/f64 mixes are rejected; unmodeled operand types are left to C#.
claim:decimal-arithmetic-type.plain: The type checker now types decimal arithmetic correctly.

claim:proof-refers-to-local.text: A §PROOF may use an immutable §B local whose definition is exactly its value at the proof (the listed rules); collisions, complex refinement predicates and operator overloads refuse it; other locals stay Unsupported with a reason; overflow-dependent proofs are Assumed and keep the runtime check (#1516).
claim:proof-refers-to-local.plain: Proofs can now mention simple local variables, under strict rules.

claim:website-conversion-guide.text: A new guide 'Converting C#: What Stays C# and Why' shows real converter output for each 0.25 family, checked in CI against the converter (complete programs compiled); the convert, migrate, MCP, feature-check, self-check and structured-output pages state each surface's defaults.
claim:website-conversion-guide.plain: The website has a new guide on converting C#, checked against the real converter.

claim:guide-corrections.text: Checking the pages found four #943 defects, fixed in the release; yield-return (methods only) is still a listed gap; docs/cli/feature-check.md no longer lists string-interpolation as fully supported.
claim:guide-corrections.plain: Writing the guide found and fixed four converter defects.

claim:website-examples-checked-in-ci.text: calor self-check docs reads website/content/**/*.mdx on every PR: complete programs must compile with no errors, and 49 programs on 96 pages are checked; examples meant to fail are labelled with their diagnostic codes; quoted output is real or labelled illustrative; diagnostic codes, keywords and versions are checked; the changelog page is excluded.
claim:website-examples-checked-in-ci.plain: Website code examples are now compiled in CI; 49 programs on 96 pages are checked.

claim:website-example-fixes.text: The check found 11 non-compiling examples, all fixed (3 labelled, 4 old syntax, 2 cross-module, 2 refinement); the baseline counted 13 including 2 fragments; 5 stale keyword references fixed; invented and impossible output replaced by checked or captured output; the refinement-type pages now say a default calor compile does not run the obligation solver (the calor_refine MCP tool does); new findings use Calor1332-Calor1334.
claim:website-example-fixes.plain: 11 broken website examples were found and fixed, and the refinement pages now say which command runs the obligation solver.

claim:array-expressions-native-ordered.text: Array creations inside expressions convert to native Calor with C# evaluation order kept (once, left to right, short-circuit preserved); new forms (inline §ARR2D with §ROW, sized §ARR2D for rank 3+, (§IDX2D g i j).Member); jagged and rectangular forms keep type and rank; new T[0] and { } create fresh arrays (#1132).
claim:array-expressions-native-ordered.plain: Arrays in expressions now convert to Calor and keep C#'s evaluation order.

claim:generated-names-avoid-collisions.text: Generated names (_hoist000, arr2d004) skip every identifier in the source and in a project migration's other files.
claim:generated-names-avoid-collisions.plain: Converter-generated names no longer clash with user names.

claim:array-shapes-stay-csharp-reported.text: Shapes that cannot be written in place stay C# and are reported (conditional-expression-hoisting, array-element-block), including collection-initializer and multi-line elements.
claim:array-shapes-stay-csharp-reported.plain: Array forms that cannot be expressed stay C# and are reported.

claim:arr2d-row-effects-charged.text: Elements of §ARR2D rows are charged for effects; array members such as GetLength and Rank on array-typed receivers remain unknown calls (Calor0410 unless declared or --permissive-effects), except System.Array receivers and manifest-defaulted element namespaces.
claim:arr2d-row-effects-charged.plain: Effects inside 2D array rows are now checked; array member calls are still unknown.

claim:trusted-publishing.text: NuGet publishing uses nuget.org Trusted Publishing; no NuGet API key is stored in GitHub; the policy requires the main-only nuget-release environment, so an older tag's workflow cannot obtain a key; on 2026-10-19 the live check reported the gap closed, with Actions workflow permissions confirmed by maintainer attestation.
claim:trusted-publishing.plain: Publishing to NuGet uses short-lived tokens, and old workflows cannot publish.

claim:notes-hash-checked-g014.text: On every run the gate checks that the candidate's notes section hashes to the adjudicated notes (G014).
claim:notes-hash-checked-g014.plain: The release notes cannot differ from the reviewed ones.

claim:benchmark-publication-separate-g01.text: Publishing a release does not publish benchmark results; that needs a separate manual run and an approval in the acceptance record (G015).
claim:benchmark-publication-separate-g01.plain: Benchmark numbers need their own explicit approval to publish.

claim:release-sdk-pin-no-google-fonts.text: Release jobs install exactly .NET SDK 10.0.401, and the website no longer fetches fonts from Google Fonts at build time.
claim:release-sdk-pin-no-google-fonts.plain: Release builds use one pinned SDK and no build-time font download.

claim:release-runtime-pinned.text: Release jobs run the C# compiler on the SDK's own runtime (10.0.12), remove any newer 10.0 runtime and fail if one remains, because the runtime version changed package bytes.
claim:release-runtime-pinned.plain: Package bytes no longer depend on which .NET runtime the build machine had.
